$comment: 0.x mode: while the major version is 0, the releaseRules below release a MINOR for a breaking change (any type with !, or a BREAKING CHANGE footer) instead of a major, so the line can evolve without a 1.0 promise. Once the packages reach 1.0, change that rule's release to "major" and drop this comment. The commit analyzer applies every rule that matches a commit and keeps the largest release, except that a matching rule with "release": false wins over all of them; so the list has no such rules (a type no rule names releases nothing), or a breaking refactor!/chore!/docs! releases nothing (the refactor! merged after v0.41.1 did not release). Deleting the breaking rule would not do either: the feat/fix rules would then give feat! a minor and fix! a patch, and the analyzer's built-in rules would give other breaking types a major. CONTRIBUTING.md states the same rule for contributors. The conventionalcommits preset (installed by the shared workflow) is what makes a bare feat!:/fix!: count as breaking; the default angular preset does not parse the marker at all.

plugins.verifyReleaseCmd: out=$(gh release view "v${nextRelease.version}" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then echo "::error::Release v${nextRelease.version} already exists; releases are immutable."; exit 1; fi; case "$out" in *"release not found"*) exit 0;; esac; echo "::error::Could not confirm that Release v${nextRelease.version} is absent (gh release view exited $rc): $out"; exit 1
plugins.prepareCmd: uv run --no-sync python scripts/set_version.py ${nextRelease.version} && uv lock && uv run --no-sync python scripts/verify_release_version.py v${nextRelease.version} && uv run --no-sync python scripts/build_wheels.py && uv run --no-sync python scripts/smoke_install_wheels.py && (cd dist && sha256sum *.whl *.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS)
